bibliographic.title: STARSS: A Spatio-Temporal Action Rating System for Soccer
bibliographic.venue: ECML/PKDD Workshop on Machine Learning and Data Mining for Sports Analytics (MLSA)

scope.rationale: STARSS is an action valuation method for soccer that splits matches into phases, assigns phase ratings based on similarity (via DTW) to historical phases that end in a goal, and distributes those ratings across individual actions. It directly fits the action-valuation / possession-value literature.

model.name: STARSS (Spatio-Temporal Action Rating System for Soccer)
inputs: event stream of actions (type, timestamp, player, team, x-y location)
outcome for shots (off target, on target, goal)
x and y coordinates of the actions making up a phase
model.target: Phase rating = proportion of the k most similar historical phases (by spatial DTW distance) that end in a goal; distributed to individual actions via exponential-decay action weights
model.architecture: k-nearest-neighbors over phases using multivariate dynamic time warping (DTW) on (x,y) action sequences; phase rating distributed across actions using an exponential-decay weighting scheme with parameter lambda
model.temporal_horizon: until end of phase (uninterrupted sequence of actions by one team; new phase on possession switch or >10 seconds gap)

data.provider: unspecified (play-by-play event data; co-author affiliated with SciSports)

evaluation.splits: Chronological / temporal: for rating a match, only matches from the same league played before the date of that match are used to discover similar phases; no held-out test split with quantitative metrics reported.

claims.statement: Dataset comprises 4253 matches, 7,569,802 game events, 110,290 shots, and 11,842 goals across the English Premier League, German Bundesliga, and Spanish La Liga for the 2012/2013 through 2015/2016 seasons.
A new phase is started each time possession switches between teams or more than 10 seconds pass between consecutive actions.

Phase rating is computed as the proportion of the k most similar historical phases (by multivariate DTW distance on (x,y) coordinates) that end in a goal; example: 13/100 similar phases ending in a goal yields rating 0.13.

Action weights are computed via exponential decay (w_i = (1 - lambda) * w_{i+1}) with the last action weight set to 1, then normalised to sum to one across the phase, so the phase rating is fully distributed across its actions.
For all case studies, parameters are set to k = 100 and lambda = 0.25 based on domain knowledge and empirical analysis.
Alexis Sanchez tops the 2015/2016 Premier League ranking with a STARSS rating per 90 of 0.289 over 2446 minutes (0.478 goals per 90, 0.147 assists per 90).
Zlatko Junuzovic tops the 2015/2016 Bundesliga ranking with a STARSS rating per 90 of 0.271 (0.153 goals per 90, 0.383 assists per 90).
Lionel Messi tops the 2015/2016 La Liga ranking with a STARSS rating per 90 of 0.387 over 2728 minutes (0.759 goals per 90, 0.528 assists per 90).
Five of the top-15 Bundesliga players play for FC Bayern Munich.
In the El Clasico of 2 April 2016, Lionel Messi contributed 19% of FC Barcelona's team STARSS rating and Gareth Bale contributed 21% of Real Madrid's team STARSS rating.
Wingers and attacking midfielders tend to contribute more to a team's STARSS rating than strikers.

Unlike most existing approaches to rate phases in soccer (which only take phases that lead to a goal or shot into account), STARSS rewards teams/players for getting the ball into dangerous places even if the phase does not lead to a shot.
